description: Why K stars were classified as M stars, and how the sky background subtraction stage fixed it (2026-09-19). Frame: M 13 spectral stack (ASI533MM Pro, 405 mm). Stars are HD/BD field stars of magnitude 6.8-9.2 with catalog types.

finding_1_residuals.method: Corrected star spectrum divided by the best-scaled reference of its catalog type, median per wavelength bin (bands excluded).
finding_1_residuals.bright_standards_A_stars: Vega, Alcor-pair star 2, g UMa: within about 6% of 1.00 at every wavelength.
finding_1_residuals.six_K_stars_as_stored: 0.6-0.8 at 4200-6000 A, about 1.0 at 6000-6800, then 1.4-1.7 at 6960-7700 and about 2.0 at 7720-8000. Same shape in every star (spread 0.14-0.38).
finding_1_residuals.HD_150679_catalog_A2: 3.3 at 7720-8000, the same kind of red excess.

finding_2_sky_share_removed_by_the_sky_s.format: share of the un-subtracted spectrum that was background, by wavelength band 4200-5400 / 5400-6800 / 6800-7400 / 7400-8000

finding_3_types_after_re_extraction_with.format: catalog type: stored result -> re-extracted with pooled-median sky subtraction -> with the lower-of-two-bands estimator (score); steps from the catalog type in brackets
finding_3_types_after_re_extraction_with.HD 150293 K0: M1V(11) -> Unknown -> M5V 0.76(15): the extraction fails for this star with either estimator (100% of its spectrum is removed as background). Not resolved; probably the trail is not being followed (star at x=85, near the left edge), not a sky-estimator problem.

decision: Lower of the two band medians (pooled median failed when a neighbour's trail filled one band). One frame, seven stars: treat as provisional.
consequence: The stored spectra of faint stars were extracted before the sky stage existed and are mostly background. They must be re-extracted from the images, not just recomputed. The earlier 7000 A upper-limit effect on K stars was this same background, which is brightest in the red.
